Extract the branch of a tree below one context

Source: R/query.R
subtree.Rd

subtree() returns the part of a fitted tree that lies below a given context: the context itself and every longer context that ends with it, that is, every history that extends it further into the past. The branch shows how the prediction after a given recent history is refined by what happened before it, and can be summarized, converted to a data frame and plotted like a full tree.

Contexts keep their full names, and the states, smoothing and other settings are those of the original tree. The printed header names the context at which the branch was cut.

Usage

subtree(tree, pathway)

Arguments

tree

A transitiontrees object.

pathway

The context at which to cut, oldest state first: a string in arrow notation or a character vector. It must be a context of the tree.

Value

A transitiontrees object holding pathway and its descendants.

Conditions

transitiontrees_bad_input when tree is not a fitted tree or pathway is not one of its contexts.

See also

pathway_exists(), query_pathway(), plot.transitiontrees().

Examples

tree <- context_tree(trajectories, max_depth = 3)
branch <- subtree(tree, "Disengaged")
summary(branch)
#> <transitiontrees summary>  11 nodes, depth <= 3, 3 states  [unpruned]
